subject.title: github-copilot: legacy OAuth token refresh sends bearer credential to unvalidated enterpriseUrl domain

question: How should OpenClaw handle persisted legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth `enterpriseUrl` values that are outside the Copilot domain allowlist before any refresh token is sent?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the permanent behavior for already-persisted legacy credentials is a security-boundary and upgrade-compatibility choice rather than a safe automated cleanup decision.

options.title: Fail closed plus doctor repair
options.body: Reject non-allowlisted domains in refresh and add doctor repair that reports or rewrites unsafe legacy `enterpriseUrl` values before runtime uses them.

options.title: Runtime fallback only
options.body: Normalize unsafe domains to `github.com` during refresh, reducing token egress risk while leaving stored legacy state for a later cleanup.

options.title: Private security workflow first
options.body: Move the follow-up into the repository security process before deciding public migration, release, and disclosure behavior.

recommendation.title: Fail closed plus doctor repair
recommendation.body: Reject non-allowlisted domains in refresh and add doctor repair that reports or rewrites unsafe legacy `enterpriseUrl` values before runtime uses them.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest available history signal for persisted auth-store ownership, while the decision itself is security-boundary policy.
